title: Little Office of S. Barbara, Virgin and Martyr, for the Purpose of Asking for a Blessed Death
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: Diffusa est gratia in labiis tuis: propterea benedixit te Deus in aeternum.
blocks.english: Grace is poured abroad in thy lips: therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine, labia mea aperies.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus, in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine, ad adjuvandum me festina.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

blocks.source: ℣. Gloria Patri. Alleluia.
blocks.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father. Alleluia.

blocks.source: A Septuagesima usque ad Pascha, loco Alleluia, dicitur: Laus tibi, Domine, Rex aeternae gloriae.
blocks.english: During Lent until Easter, instead of the alleluia the following is said: Praise to Thee, O Lord, King of everlasting glory.
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from an identical complete Latin passage elsewhere in this PDF. This office’s source transcription has also been compared with its printed PDF pages. The original Latin says Septuagesima; the supplied English says Lent. These differing printed terms are retained.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Fatalis o agonis Patrona Barbara, Coelestibus coronis, Gemmisque fulgida! Moerentis in novissimo Mors certa spiculo Sed, Virgo, te favente, Sum par periculo.
blocks.english:
O Barbara, patroness of the final struggle,
Shining with heavenly crowns and gems!
Death is certain with its last dart of sorrow,
But, O Virgin, with thy favour I am equal to the danger.

blocks.source: Ant. Osee. 2. 19. Sponsabo te mihi in sempiternum; et sponsabo te mihi in justitia et judicio, et in misericordia, et in miserationibus.
blocks.english: Ant. Osee 2:19. I will espouse thee to Me for ever; and I will espouse thee to Me in justice and judgment, and in mercy and compassion.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis, sancta Virgo et Martyr Barbara.
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint Barbara, virgin and martyr.

blocks.source: ℟. Ut felix nobis sit mortis hora.
blocks.english: ℟. That the hour of our death may be blessed.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Intercessio, quaesumus, Domine, sanctae virginis et martyris tuae Barbarae nos adjuvet: ut qui ejus patrocinio in angustiis et necessitatibus nostris imploramus, auxilium quoque in hora potissimum mortis experiarmur. Per Dominum nostrum.
blocks.english: May the intercession of Thy holy virgin and martyr Barbara help us, we beseech Thee, O Lord: that we who implore her patronage in our straits and necessities may also experience her help, above all at the hour of death. Through our Lord.
blocks.editorialNote: The Latin has irregular “qui ejus patrocinio” and “experiarmur”; the English expresses the apparent request for Saint Barbara’s help, while retaining the printed Latin.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine, exaudi orationem meam.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

blocks.source: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.
blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.

blocks.source: ℣. Benedicamus Domino.
blocks.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Deo gratias.
blocks.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

blocks.source: ℣. Fidelium animae per misericordiam Dei requiescant in pace.
blocks.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

blocks.source: ℟. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. Amen.

blocks.source: Tu vincis innocenti Candore lilia, Per prata quae nitenti Stant lacte turgida. Da candido nitore Ut, Virgo, fulgeam, Castoque fac amore Ut purus ardeam.
blocks.english:
In innocent whiteness thou surpassest the lilies
That stand in the meadows, full of shining milky brightness.
Grant that I may shine with pure radiance, O Virgin,
And make me burn in chaste love, pure of heart.

blocks.source: Ant. Cant. 8. 7. Aquae multae non potuerunt extinguere charitatem, nec flumina obruent illam.
blocks.english: Ant. Canticles 8:7. Many waters have not been able to extinguish charity, neither shall rivers overwhelm it.

blocks.source: Dum proprio cruore Asperas pingeris, Vincis rosas rubore, Quae stant in hortulis. O coelico vireto Plantatae flosculae! Hoc orbis in vepreto, Me, quaeso, respice.
blocks.english:
While thou art harshly stained with thine own blood,
Thou surpassest in redness the roses that stand in gardens.
O little flower planted in a heavenly garden,
Look upon me, I beseech thee, amid this world’s thorns.

blocks.source: Ant. Sap. 3. 13. Haec est quae nescivit thorum in delicto, habebit fructum in respectu animarum sanctarum.
blocks.english: Ant. Wisdom 3:13. This is she who knew not the bed in sin; she shall have fruit at the visitation of holy souls.

blocks.source: Ut axe sunt sereno Nocturna sidera, Ut vere sunt amoeno Jucunda flumina; Sic, Virgo, charitatis Es luce fulgida, Sic, Virgo, puritatis Es rore limpida.
blocks.english:
As the stars by night are in the clear sky,
As pleasant rivers are in lovely spring,
So, O Virgin, thou art bright with the light of charity;
So, O Virgin, thou art clear with the dew of purity.

blocks.source: Ant. Sap. 4. 1. O quam pulchra est casta generatio cum claritate! immortalis est enim memoria illius; quoniam et apud Deum nota est, et apud homines.
blocks.english: Ant. Wisdom 4:1. O how beautiful is the chaste generation with glory! For its memory is immortal, since it is known both with God and with men.

blocks.source: Te sentiunt patronam Quos morbus opprimit, Te sublevare pronam Quos cura deserit. Angore cum super me Me morbus opprimit; Succurre, quando nemo Levamen adferet.
blocks.english:
Those oppressed by sickness know thee as their patroness;
Those whom care has abandoned know thee ready to help.
When sickness presses me with anguish,
Come to my aid when no one will bring relief.

blocks.source: Ant. Eccli. 51. 4. Liberasti me secundum multitudinem misericordiae nominis tui de manibus quaerentium animam meam, et de portis tribulationum, quae circumdederunt me.
blocks.english: Ant. Ecclesiasticus 51:4. Thou hast delivered me according to the abundance of the mercy of Thy name, from the hands of those who sought my life and from the gates of tribulations that surrounded me.

blocks.source: Cum ferreo sopore Mors membra vinciet, Et tartarus furore Bacchante saeviet: Dum Judicis severi Tribunal horreo, Tum, Virgo, me tuere Ne differ, obsecro.
blocks.english:
When death binds my limbs in an iron sleep
And hell rages with furious frenzy;
When I dread the tribunal of the stern Judge,
Then, O Virgin, protect me; delay not, I beseech thee.

blocks.source: Ant. Matth. 25. 6. Media nocte clamor factus est: Ecce sponsus venit, exite obviam ei.
blocks.english: Ant. Matthew 25:6. At midnight a cry was made: Behold, the bridegroom comes; go forth to meet him.

blocks.source: Amabo te, sanabo, Dum vita manserit, Magisque praedicabo, Cum vita cessaverit: Interque liliata Cum me receperis, Queis gaudiis repleta, O Virgo, pasceris.
blocks.english:
I shall love thee and heal thee while life remains,
And proclaim thee still more when life has ceased;
When thou hast received me among the lilies,
O Virgin, what joys, with which thou art filled, shall nourish thee!
blocks.editorialNote: Both the attached PDF and the cited 1879 Coeleste Palmetum, printed p.281 (scan PDF p.311), print “sanabo”, I shall heal. This English now follows that literal printed verb. The earlier conjectural “sing thy praises” is withdrawn. The unusual address is retained; no intended alternative Latin verb is supplied.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish:
I shall love thee and sing thy praises while life remains,
And proclaim thee still more when life has ceased;
When thou hast received me among the lilies,
O Virgin, what joys, with which thou art filled, shall nourish thee!

blocks.source: Ant. Cant. 2. 11, 13. Jam hiems transiit, imber abiit et recessit: Surge, amica mea, speciosa mea, et veni.
blocks.english: Ant. Canticles 2:11,13. Now winter has passed, the rain has gone and departed: arise, my friend, my fair one, and come.

blocks.source: Admitte nostra vota, O sancta Barbara, Profectam mente tota, Patrona maxima: Exoptote te videre, Cum cesso vivere; Tunc, oro, me tuere, Coeloque suscipe. Amen.
blocks.english:
Receive our vows, O Saint Barbara,
Offered with our whole mind, O mighty patroness.
I long to see thee when I cease to live;
Then, I pray, protect me and receive me into heaven. Amen.

editorialNotes.text: All three attached PDF pages were visually reviewed. The seven printed hours and Oblatio remain; repeated versicle/collect groups expand from this office’s Matins. Compline’s sanabo was also checked in the cited 1879 edition p.281, and is now rendered literally as heal rather than conjecturally sing. Printed wording, including the unusual address, is retained. The differing supplied seasonal terms Lent/Septuagesima remain documented.
